title: Proving a quadrilateral is a parallelogram
problem: $ABCD$ is a quadrilateral. $P$, $Q$, $R$, $S$ are the midpoints of $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DA$ respectively. Prove $PQRS$ is a parallelogram.

steps.instruction: Write position vectors for the midpoints.
Conclude from the equality of the side vectors.
steps.working: Since $\overrightarrow{PQ} = \overrightarrow{SR}$, sides $PQ$ and $SR$ are parallel and equal in length. Therefore $PQRS$ is a parallelogram. $\square$

title: Angle in a semicircle
problem: A circle has centre $O$ at the origin and radius $r$. Diameter $AB$ has $A = -r\mathbf{i}$, $B = r\mathbf{i}$. $P$ is any point on the circle with $|\mathbf{p}| = r$. Prove $\angle APB = 90°$.

steps.instruction: Write the vectors from $P$ to $A$ and from $P$ to $B$.
Apply the difference of squares identity $(\mathbf{u}+\mathbf{v})\cdot(\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{v}) = |\mathbf{u}|^2-|\mathbf{v}|^2$.
Conclude from the dot product being zero.
steps.working: Since the dot product is zero, $\angle APB = 90°$. $\square$

answer: $\angle APB = 90°$ for any point $P$ on the circle.

title: Medians of a triangle are concurrent
problem: Triangle $ABC$ has position vectors $\mathbf{a}$, $\mathbf{b}$, $\mathbf{c}$. Show all three medians meet at $G = \frac{\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}+\mathbf{c}}{3}$.

steps.working: The median from $A$ goes to $M = \frac{\mathbf{b}+\mathbf{c}}{2}$, the midpoint of $BC$.

steps.instruction: Find the point dividing $AM$ in ratio $2:1$ from $A$.
Use symmetry to extend the result to the other two medians.
steps.working: By symmetry, the same calculation from $B$ (to the midpoint of $AC$) and from $C$ (to the midpoint of $AB$) also gives $\frac{\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}+\mathbf{c}}{3}$.
All three medians pass through $G$, so they are concurrent. $\square$

answer: All three medians meet at $G=\dfrac{\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}+\mathbf{c}}{3}$, so they are concurrent.
